Bone resorption is increased after running, with no change in bone formation. Feeding during exercise might attenuate this increase, preventing associated problems for bone. This study investigated the immediate and short-term bone metabolic responses to carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during treadmill running. Ten men completed two 7-day trials, once being fed CHO (8% glucose immediately before, every 20 min during, and immediately after exercise at a rate of 0.7 g CHO·kg body mass −1 ·h −1 ) and once being fed placebo (PBO). On day 4 of each trial, participants completed a 120-min treadmill run at 70% of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇ o 2 max ). Blood was taken at baseline (BASE), immediately after exercise (EE), after 60 (R1) and 120 (R2) min of recovery, and on three follow-up days (FU1-FU3). Markers of bone resorption [COOH-terminal telopeptide region of collagen type 1 (β-CTX)] and formation [NH 2 -terminal propeptides of procollagen type 1 (P1NP)] were measured, along with osteocalcin (OC), parathyroid hormone (PTH), albumin-adjusted calcium (ACa), phosphate, glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2), interleukin-6 (IL-6), insulin, cortisol, leptin, and osteoprotogerin (OPG). Area under the curve was calculated in terms of the immediate (BASE, EE, R1, and R2) and short-term (BASE, FU1, FU2, and FU3) responses to exercise. β-CTX, P1NP, and IL-6 responses to exercise were significantly lower in the immediate postexercise period with CHO feeding compared with PBO (β-CTX: P = 0.028; P1NP: P = 0.021; IL-6: P = 0.036), although there was no difference in the short-term response (β-CTX: P = 0.856; P1NP: P = 0.721; IL-6: P = 0.327). No other variable was significantly affected by CHO feeding during exercise. We conclude that CHO feeding during exercise attenuated the β-CTX and P1NP responses in the hours but not days following exercise, indicating an acute effect of CHO feeding on bone turnover. carbohydrate feeding bone metabolism running exercise feeding influences the circadian rhythm of bone metabolism at rest ( 21 ). Markers of bone resorption decrease after mixed-meal feeding ( 3 ) and ingestion of individual macronutrients at rest ( 1 , 7 ). Reductions in bone resorption occur after oral but not parenteral administration of glucose, suggesting that enteric hormones might play a part in mediating the effects of glucose on bone metabolism ( 1 ). This is supported by studies showing that administration of octreotide, an inhibitor of enteric hormone secretion, abolishes the reduction in bone resorption following glucose ingestion ( 4 ). These findings suggest a potential means to modulate bone turnover by nutritional strategies or through manipulation of dietary composition ( 25 ). Exhaustive weight-bearing exercise increases bone resorption by 40–45% for up to four consecutive days without a concomitant increase in bone formation, potentially resulting in a short-term net loss of bone ( 19 ). Attenuating bone resorption is a potential countermeasure to the bone uncoupling shown to occur with exercise that might predispose athletes and military recruits to stress fractures and other associated injuries ( 26 ). Feeding practices, before, during, and after exercise, influence the interaction between exercise and bone turnover, making them potentially important for offsetting bone loss. Scott et al. ( 22 ) showed that feeding a mixed meal prior to exercise reduced COOH-terminal telopeptide region of collagen type 1 (β-CTX) concentrations before a 60-min treadmill run, although the subsequent increase in β-CTX during exercise was similar in fed and fasted groups. This indicated a novel interaction between feeding, exercise, and bone metabolism that requires further study, particularly in relation to feeding practices during and after exercise. Carbohydrate (CHO), fat, and protein all decrease β-CTX ( 3 , 4 ); CHO ingestion during exercise is an established nutritional practice for athletes, proven to enhance physical performance and exercise capacity by providing additional fuel to the muscle ( 11 ). A recent study ( 5 ) suggests that CHO is a candidate nutrient for modulating bone resorption during an exercise program (8-day intensive training), although factors that may have mediated these responses were not examined. The aim of this study was to investigate the responses of bone metabolism to CHO feeding during exercise in the hours (immediate) and days (short term) following a single bout of strenuous treadmill running. We also measured markers associated with feeding, exercise, and bone to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the immediate and short-term bone metabolic responses to carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running (120-min at 70% V̇o2max) in healthy men. It found that CHO feeding during exercise acutely attenuated the post-exercise increases in bone resorption (β-CTX) and bone formation (P1NP) markers, as well as reduced Interleukin-6 (IL-6) elevation, in the hours immediately following exercise, but these effects did not persist in the subsequent days, suggesting a potential strategy to minimize acute exercise-induced bone resorption and influence bone turnover.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during prolonged treadmill running
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Ten men completed two 7-day trials, one with CHO feeding and one with placebo (PBO). On day 4, participants completed a 120-min treadmill run at 70% of maximal oxygen consumption (V̇o2max). In the CHO trial, an 8% glucose solution was ingested immediately before, every 20 minutes during, and immediately after exercise, at a rate of 0.7 g CHO·kg body mass−1·h−1 (approximately 50 g/h), totaling 102.1 ± 10.6 g glucose in 1,276 ± 132 ml solution. The PBO trial involved equal volumes of a taste-matched flavored water. No dose-response comparisons were reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: COOH-terminal telopeptide region of collagen type 1 (β-CTX)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the PBO trial, β-CTX increased by between 6% and 14% from baseline (BASE: 0.54 ± 0.14 ng/ml) to follow-up days (FU3: 0.61 ± 0.16 ng/ml). The AUC analysis showed a significantly lower β-CTX response in the immediate post-exercise period with CHO feeding compared to PBO (P = 0.028), indicating an attenuation of the exercise-induced increase. No significant difference was found in the short-term response over follow-up days (P = 0.856).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Marker of bone resorption (collagen degradation product).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate post-exercise and short-term recovery following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with or without carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bone turnover and specifically bone resorption level. Lower levels with CHO feeding suggest reduced exercise-induced bone breakdown, potentially minimizing bone damage and offering a countermeasure to exercise-induced bone uncoupling that can lead to stress fractures.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the PBO trial, P1NP was 5–14% higher on follow-up days (FU1: 67.9 ± 33.2 ng/ml, FU2: 66.2 ± 31.7 ng/ml, FU3: 68.4 ± 28.0 ng/ml) than at BASE (63.1 ± 30.5 ng/ml). AUC analysis showed significantly lower P1NP concentrations in the CHO trial compared with the PBO trial in the hours following exercise (P = 0.021), indicating an attenuation of the exercise-induced increase. No significant differences were observed over follow-up days (P = 0.721).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Marker of bone formation (procollagen type I N-terminal propeptide).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate post-exercise and short-term recovery following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with or without carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates bone turnover and specifically bone formation level. Lower levels with CHO feeding suggest an acute effect on bone turnover and maintenance of dynamic balance between resorption and formation, potentially contributing to reduced overall bone turnover.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the PBO trial, exercise caused a significant elevation (223% increase, P < 0.001) in IL-6. CHO feeding significantly attenuated this elevation immediately after exercise (P = 0.036). These differences did not persist over follow-up days (P = 0.327). A strong correlation (r = 0.74, P < 0.05) was observed between the immediate responses of IL-6 and β-CTX in the CHO trial.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine, involved in immune response and energy metabolism. It is an activator of osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption, capable of stimulating osteoclast differentiation and activity in the presence of sIL-6Rs.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate post-exercise period following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with or without carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Attenuation by CHO feeding suggests a reduction in exercise-induced inflammation and is identified as a possible mediator explaining the reduction in β-CTX concentrations and the short-term effect of CHO ingestion on bone metabolism.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Not affected by exercise in the PBO trial or by CHO ingestion during exercise in the immediate (P = 0.343) or short-term (P = 0.786) recovery periods. No concomitant effect on circulating OC concentrations with CHO feeding during exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Hormone involved in bone formation and mineralization, a marker of coupled bone turnover, capable of suppressing IL-6 release, and important in the relationship between bone remodeling and energy metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after strenuous exercise (120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max) with PBO or CHO feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant indicator in this context, suggesting stable osteocalcin levels regardless of exercise or CHO intake, and it was not involved in the observed effects of CHO feeding on bone turnover.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased then returned to baseline (PBO trial), unchanged (with CHO)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the PBO trial, PTH increased significantly (P < 0.001) by 87% immediately after exercise (6.6 ± 2.0 pmol/l vs BASE 3.7 ± 1.2 pmol/l), then returned towards baseline and was slightly lower at R1 (3.6 ± 1.2 pmol/l) and R2 (3.3 ± 1.3 pmol/l). No immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding observed.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates calcium and phosphate levels in the blood, primarily by increasing calcium, and is involved in bone turnover.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after strenuous exercise (120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max) with PBO or CHO feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the body's response to maintain calcium homeostasis during exercise-induced stress. Unlikely to be a mediator of the effects of CHO supplementation on bone turnover, as no alterations due to CHO were observed.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No exercise effect was shown for albumin-adjusted calcium in the PBO trial (P = 0.871). No immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding observed.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Maintains calcium homeostasis in the blood; calcium is an essential mineral for bone health and numerous physiological processes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after strenuous exercise (120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max) with PBO or CHO feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates stable circulating calcium levels during exercise under these conditions. Unlikely to be a mediator of the effects of CHO supplementation on bone turnover, as no alterations were observed in calcium metabolism.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: increased then returned to baseline (PBO trial), unchanged (with CHO)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the PBO trial, phosphate increased significantly (P < 0.001) by 21% immediately after exercise (1.4 ± 0.1 mmol/l vs BASE 1.1 ± 0.1 mmol/l), then returned to baseline values by R1 (1.1 ± 0.2 mmol/l). No immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding observed.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Essential for bone mineralization, energy metabolism (ATP), and cell function. Phosphate is an essential mineral for bone health and numerous physiological processes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During and after strenuous exercise (120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max) with PBO or CHO feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects electrolyte and metabolic shifts during exercise. Unlikely to be a mediator of the effects of CHO supplementation on bone turnover, as no alterations due to CHO were observed in phosphate metabolism.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant effect by carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during exercise compared to placebo. CHO did not significantly alter the immediate or short-term responses of GLP-2 to exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Associated with feeding, exercise, and bone. Peptide hormone involved in intestinal growth and nutrient absorption.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate and short-term post-exercise following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Indicates that intestinal function markers were not significantly impacted by the exercise or CHO intervention. Unlikely to be responsible for the effect of CHO supplementation on bone turnover.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: significant effect of exercise (PBO trial), unchanged (with CHO)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant effects of exercise (PBO trial) were shown (P < 0.001). No other immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding on this modulator. CHO did not significantly alter the immediate or short-term responses of insulin to exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Associated with feeding, exercise, and bone. Regulates blood glucose levels and promotes anabolic processes/energy metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate and short-term post-exercise following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Reflects the metabolic response and glucose regulation during exercise. Unlikely to be responsible for the effect of CHO supplementation on bone turnover.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant effect by carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during exercise compared to placebo. No significant effects of exercise or CHO feeding reported. CHO did not significantly alter the immediate or short-term responses of cortisol to exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Associated with feeding, exercise, and bone. Stress hormone involved in metabolism, immune response, and bone turnover.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate and short-term post-exercise following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Indicates the adrenal stress response to exercise; stable levels suggest the exercise or intervention did not significantly alter the overall stress hormone profile. Unlikely to be responsible for the effect of CHO supplementation on bone turnover.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: significant effect of exercise (PBO trial), unchanged (with CHO)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant effects of exercise (PBO trial) were shown (P < 0.01). No other immediate or short-term effects of CHO feeding on this modulator. CHO did not significantly alter the immediate or short-term responses of leptin to exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Associated with feeding, exercise, and bone. Hormone regulating energy balance, appetite, and bone metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate and short-term post-exercise following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Indicates the metabolic and hormonal response to exercise, potentially influencing energy expenditure and bone health. Unlikely to be responsible for the effect of CHO supplementation on bone turnover.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant effect by carbohydrate (CHO) feeding during exercise compared to placebo. No significant effects of exercise or CHO feeding reported. No effect of CHO feeding on circulating OPG concentrations.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Associated with feeding, exercise, and bone. Regulator of bone resorption, acts as a decoy receptor for RANKL.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Immediate and short-term post-exercise following a 120-min treadmill run at 70% V̇o2max with carbohydrate feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Measured to explore possible mediating and mechanistic factors related to bone metabolism. Indicates stable regulation of bone resorption by OPG during exercise, unaffected by CHO feeding. Not a mediator of the observed effects in this study.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged with PBO, significantly elevated with CHO
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: PBO feeding: BASE 4.7 ± 0.3 mmol/l, EE 4.8 ± 0.8 mmol/l. CHO feeding: significantly elevated (P = 0.002) at EE (6.3 ± 0.6 mmol/l) compared to BASE (4.9 ± 0.2 mmol/l). CHO trial was significantly (P < 0.001) higher than PBO trial at EE.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primary energy source, regulated by insulin, central to energy metabolism during exercise.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: During strenuous exercise with PBO or CHO feeding.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates availability of carbohydrates for energy during exercise and the impact of CHO supplementation on glycemic response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly from BASE to EE (P = 0.002).
